findings.title: update() uses the org-aware wrapped model for login-cache invalidation decisions, which can mask real eligibility changes
findings.body: In update(), `idpById` is obtained via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which is the cache-aware method of this same class and therefore wraps the result with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel(...)`. That wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to also factor in the live state of the linked organization (`org.isEnabled()`), while the underlying `getForLogin()` query that actually populates the cached ID list filters strictly on the IDP's raw, persisted `enabled` column (via `LoginFilter`), independent of the organization's current status. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model)` then calls `getLoginPredicate().test(idpById)`, which invokes the wrapped (live) `isEnabled()`. If the linked organization happens to be disabled at the moment of the update, `idpById.isEnabled()` returns false even though the IDP's raw `enabled` flag (and therefore its actual membership in the cached login ID list) is true. Comparing this masked value against the predicate result for the raw `model` passed to update() can make the method wrongly conclude that login-eligibility 'didn't change' (both evaluate false) when in fact the IDP's raw eligibility did change (e.g. toggling hideOnLogin), causing the login caches to be left stale instead of invalidated. Note that remove() correctly avoids this by using `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` (the raw, unwrapped delegate) rather than the cache/organization-aware getById(); update() should do the same for consistency and correctness.

findings.title: remove() now always performs an extra backend lookup for the IDP by alias, even when not needed
findings.body: Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only invoked inside the `if (isInvalid(cacheKey))` branch when a backend lookup was actually required. The refactor moved this call out to the top of remove(), so `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is now executed unconditionally on every removal, even when the cache entry is still valid and already available via `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, ...)`. This adds an unnecessary delegate/DB round trip to every identity-provider removal purely to support the new login-cache invalidation check, instead of reusing the already-available cached model when present.

findings.title: Login cache sub-key is unnecessarily split by organizationId for FetchMode.REALM_ONLY
findings.body: `getForLogin` computes `searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""` and stores results in the per-mode `IdentityProviderListQuery` under that sub-key, regardless of fetch mode. However, for `FetchMode.REALM_ONLY` the default `getForLogin` implementation completely ignores `organizationId` (it forces `ORGANIZATION_ID=null` in the search options), so the result is identical for any organizationId value. If `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, orgA)` and `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, orgB)` are both invoked, they will be cached as two separate sub-entries with identical content, causing redundant delegate queries and unnecessary cache growth instead of reusing a single REALM_ONLY entry.

findings.title: Test cleanup removes a non-existent IDP alias instead of the one actually created
findings.body: In the new `testCacheIDPForLogin` test, after creating identity providers with aliases like "idp-alias-" + i (and later "idp-alias-20"), cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` (also repeated at the idp-alias-20 creation point). The literal string "alias" is passed instead of the actual alias that was created, so the cleanup action targets a non-existent identity provider named "alias" rather than the ones actually created by the test. As a result, none of the up-to-21 identity providers created by this test are properly removed during cleanup, leaking realm state across test runs/test methods and risking alias-conflict failures or inflated counts in subsequent tests that rely on a clean realm/IDP set.
